title: A resized component keeps its pieces where they belong
goal: Drag a button out of the Library, make it wider, and its label no longer sits in the middle. Resizing scales where things sit, which is wrong for a label that should stay centred and for a background that should stretch. A container should say how its contents line up by default, for example centre everything, and any single piece inside should be able to say something different for itself, for example stretch to fill or stick to the left edge. Then a component survives being resized.
notes: Reported by the user on 2026-09-03 after dragging a built-in button onto the canvas and resizing it: the text does not stay centred; the parent should have child alignment settings that provide defaults, and children should have their own alignment settings. Root cause of what they saw: resize-a-group-and-the-pieces-inside-follow (done 2026-09-03) scales the layout proportionally but deliberately does not scale type, so a label that was centred lands off centre at any new width. Proportional scaling is the wrong rule for a container; alignment is the right one. This is the constraints model the design study describes in ui-grid.html (Horizontal: Left, Centre, Right, Stretch; Vertical: Top, Centre, Bottom, Stretch), expressed as the user asks for it: the container carries the default and a child may override. Write the decision into docs/design/ui-building.md as the resize rule, replacing the scale-the-layout rule that task recorded, and say what happens to a piece that is both stretched and rotated. Related open task one-layer-lines-up-inside-the-frame-it-sits-in is a one-shot Arrange action against a frame; this task is the persistent version, so fold that one in or make it depend on this. Auto-layout (a container that stacks and spaces its children) stays deferred per the spec; this is placement only.
acceptance: A group or frame has an alignment setting for its contents, horizontal and vertical, and every piece inside follows it when the container is resized
A single layer inside can set its own horizontal and vertical behaviour, which wins over the container default, and the inspector shows when a piece is following the default and when it is overriding
Stretch is one of the choices, so a background inside a button fills the new width while the label stays centred
Dragging a built-in button wider keeps its label centred and its background filling, with no manual fixing
Existing documents open unchanged: a layer with no setting behaves exactly as it does today
Core logic is covered by tests in PhotonzCore written before the implementation
Audit written under queue/audits/ showing a button at three widths, and anything rough filed as a follow-up
